stemMd:
The passage states which of the following about the sediment that an estuary erodes from its own bed and banks?

Consider each choice separately and select **all** that apply.
instructionsMd: Select all that apply. There is no credit for a partially correct selection.

options.label: A
options.textMd: In some estuaries it amounts to more than the rivers supply.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Vogel's measurements did not record it.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is renewed at approximately the rate at which it is drawn down.

explanationMd:
Scoring is all-or-nothing, so treat each statement as its own true-or-false question and refuse to select anything you cannot pin to a specific clause. The whole item lives in the third paragraph.

**"Vogel's measurements did not record it" — stated.** "Measuring at the head of tide records what the rivers deliver, **not** what the estuary erodes from its own bed and banks." The head of tide is where Vogel's survey took its readings, so by the passage's own description her measurements excluded this material. The next sentence removes any doubt: "Vogel accepts the omission." Both sides of the dispute agree on this point, so it is not merely the critics' allegation. **Select it.**

**"It is renewed at approximately the rate at which it is drawn down" — not stated, and denied.** Vogel's reply is that the internal supply "draws down a finite stock **rather than being renewed**." Nobody in the passage claims it is renewed at any rate, let alone at the rate it is consumed. There is no clause to point to, so it cannot be selected. **Leave it.**

**"In some estuaries it amounts to more than the rivers supply" — stated.** "In some systems that internal supply exceeds the riverine one." That is the passage's own sentence, not a claim it attributes to one party; "in some systems" and "in some estuaries" are the same restriction. **Select it.**

**The answer is the two statements about Vogel's measurements and about exceeding the rivers' supply.**

**How to check.** Name the clause for every statement you select and the clause you are contradicting for every statement you reject. If a statement is only *consistent* with the passage rather than *asserted* by it, leave it unselected: consistency is not support, and on an all-or-nothing item one generous selection costs the whole question. Note also that the statement about Vogel's measurements turns on knowing where the survey measured — the phrase "at the head of tide" appears in paragraph two and is picked up in paragraph three — so this item rewards carrying a detail across paragraphs.

distractorRationale.c: This is the opposite of what the passage says. Vogel's reply rests on the internal supply drawing down a finite stock rather than being renewed, which is exactly why she holds that it can postpone a sediment deficit without preventing one. If the supply were renewed as fast as it was consumed, her reply would collapse, so no reading of the passage supports this statement.

accessibilityText: Question about the passage on salt-marsh accretion and the sediment budget: select every statement the passage makes about the sediment an estuary erodes from its own bed and banks. The three statements are that Vogel's measurements did not record it, that it is renewed at approximately the rate at which it is drawn down, and that in some estuaries it amounts to more than the rivers supply. Consider each choice separately. Select all that apply; there is no credit for a partially correct selection.

provenance.notes: Original Reading Comprehension item in the GRE select-one-or-more-of-three format, on the original passage gre-rc-marsh-accretion-300. Written for the wave 4 top-up as a clean replacement for the quarantined item gre-verbal-rc-commonplace-registers-221. That item failed because its option B rested on a passage sentence whose subject (borrowing) was not the subject the option named (reading), so a second answer became defensible. Here every option is deliberately anchored to a sentence in the passage's own narrative voice, with no gap between what the sentence is about and what the option asserts. Not adapted from any ETS item.

review.author: gre-wave4-author
review.notes: Author solved as A and C. Uniqueness argument, written against the failure mode that quarantined gre-verbal-rc-commonplace-registers-221: (A) is anchored to 'Measuring at the head of tide records what the rivers deliver, not what the estuary erodes from its own bed and banks', reinforced by 'Vogel accepts the omission', so it is agreed by both parties and not a contested attribution; (C) is anchored to the narrator's clause 'in some systems that internal supply exceeds the riverine one', which is stated by the passage rather than attributed to the critics, and the option repeats its hedge ('in some estuaries') so no overgeneralisation is introduced; (B) is the explicit negation of 'draws down a finite stock rather than being renewed', so it is not merely unsupported but contradicted. The stem says 'states' rather than 'supports' so that a reader cannot defend an option on a chain of plausible inference. Awaiting blind independent solve; the author must not publish own work. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
